{{Top}}
{{Youmay|the type of [[Warship/Legends|warship]]|the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] or the song "[[Star Destroyer (song)|Star Destroyer]]"|linebreak=1}}
[[File:ISD_arrow.jpg|thumb|right|250px|An [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]], second generation of the Galactic Empire's signature vessel]]
{{Quote|At that close range, we won't last long against those Star Destroyers!|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Ackbar]], during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]|<ref name="Episode 6">{{Film|VI}}</ref>}}
'''Star Destroyer''' was a term used to describe a certain type of medium-sized<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref> [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]]<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations1">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> used by various factions such as the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]], the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], the [[Alliance-in-exile]], the [[Fel Empire]], [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] and the [[Galactic Federation Triumvirate]]. It was also used to describe heavily armed warships in general.<ref name="SOTG07">[[Starships of the Galaxy (Saga Edition)|''Starships of the Galaxy'', Saga Edition]]</ref>

The term originated with the idea of a warship powerful enough to destroy entire [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], and did not necessarily indicate a [[Destroyer/Legends|destroyer]] type vessel.<ref name="SOTG07" /> Despite this, Star Destroyers were sometimes referred to as destroyers themselves. One such Star Destroyer was the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] of the Galactic Republic. In the [[Anaxes War College System/Legends|Anaxes War College System]], any warship that was between 1 and 2 kilometers in length qualifies as a Star Destroyer, excepting cases where the vessel, despite its length matching that of a [[Heavy cruiser/Legends|heavy cruiser]] or [[Battlecruiser/Legends|battlecruiser]], had less or more armaments than their class or role. Examples include the 900m [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-series]] of Star Destroyer and the 2.2km [[Secutor-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Secutor''-class Star Destroyer]]. Ships with a dagger profile that fall into the Battlecruiser or Dreadnaught classes are referred to as [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyers]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:Class_II.jpg|thumb|left|250px|While not technically Star Destroyers, ships like the [[Imperial II-class frigate|''Imperial II''-class frigate]], the [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Immobilizer 418 cruiser]] or the [[Victory II-class frigate|''Victory II''-class frigate]] possessed the typical characteristic of such vessels - a wedge shaped hull and command tower.]]
The term originated within the Old Republic and referred to ships capable of destroying entire star systems with their heavy firepower. The dagger-shape was said to facilitate the ease of this by focusing the firepower forward. Any vessel that conformed to this design, could be considered a class of Star Destroyer.<ref name="SOTG07" /> Even so, many models were designed with their heavy guns aimed to the sides of the vessel, obstructing each other's line-of-sight in other directions.<ref name="Star Wars: Incredible Cross-Sections">''[[Star Wars: Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

In stricter terms, Star Destroyers were the relatively common warships that dwarfed the [[Frigate/Legends|frigates]] and [[Cruiser/Legends|cruisers]] of one of the Galactic Empire's standard [[Warship/Legends|warship]] scales,<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook1">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref><ref name="Star Wars: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> and were smaller than Imperial [[Star Cruiser/Legends|Star Cruisers]].<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations1" /> Based on descriptions of the Star Dreadnought [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], the Imperial Star Destroyer/Star Cruiser cut-off point lay somewhere around a length of 3.8 kilometers.<ref name="AGTTSWU1st">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]'', the size of the ''Executor'' was described as "five times larger than any Star Destroyer in the Imperial fleet", and length is often used as the dimension that determines ship-size in SW books.</ref> Destroyers could usually carry 10,000 or more people aboard it.

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], Star Destroyers were considered medium-weight warships.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> With the increase in warship-sizes during the time of the Empire, Star Destroyers were sometimes denoted as smaller vessels in the Imperial Navy.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations1" /> In combat, Star Destroyers usually surpassed contemporary destroyer designs, similar to how the [[Frigate/Legends|star frigates]] eclipsed most contemporary frigate classes.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> The Star Destroyer designation was usually used for warships ranging from about 500 meters<ref name="Star Wars: Droids">''[[Star Wars: Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO]]''</ref><ref name="TFUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> to about 3.8 kilometers in length,<ref name="AGTTSWU1st" /><ref name="Attack of the Clones: Incredible Cross-Sections1">''[[Star Wars: Attack of the Clones Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref><ref name="Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire">''[[Dark Forces: Soldier for the Empire]]''</ref> but the general term was used for much larger vessels as well.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook1" />

After the formation of the Anaxes War College System during the early stages of the Galactic Empire, Star Destroyers were classified as generally being between 1000 to 2000 meters in length. However, if the ship in question has fewer weapons than its standard class and the ship is larger (eg, the 2,200 meter ''Secutor''-class Star Destroyer), that ship will be classified as a Star Destroyer.<ref name="TEGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

In the time of the [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|second Galactic Empire]], Star Destroyers were described as some of the largest and most powerful warships of the time, taking some design-cues from Star Dreadnoughts like the ''Executor''-class<ref name="SOTG07" /> and performing the roles of large battleships despite their compact frame.<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0]]</ref> Many Star Destroyer classes throughout the various eras doubled as [[Carrier/Legends|carriers]].<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> In these cases, they often contained one or several [[Fighter wing/Legends|wings]] of [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]].<ref name="Star Wars: Incredible Cross-Sections" /><ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" />

==History==
===Early designs===
[[File:Leviathan_Ebon_Hawk.png|thumb|250px|A [[Republic Sienar Systems/Legends|Republic Sienar Systems]] ''Interdictor''-class cruiser circa [[3956 BBY]].]]
[[File:Imperial_navy.jpg|thumb|250px|A fleet of [[Harrower-class dreadnought|''Harrower''-class dreadnoughts]] circa [[3681 BBY]].]]
The use of wedge-shaped warships seems to be an ancient trend, dating as far back as over four millennia before the rise of the Galactic Empire. The designs were not limited to any one culture, having been observed frequently in both [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]<ref name="KOTORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> and [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] navies.<ref name="T11">{{TORweb|url=holonet/galactic-history|text=Timeline 11: Rebirth of the Sith Empire|int=Timeline 11: Rebirth of the Sith Empire}}</ref><ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

During the [[Mandalorian Wars]] [[3963 BBY|3,963 years before]] the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], a [[Mandalorian warship (Venator-style)|''Venator''-like warship]] was used by the fleets of the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]].<ref name="KOTOR17">[[Knights of the Old Republic 17|''Knights of the Old Republic'' 17]]</ref>
During the same conflicts, the wedge-shaped [[Interdictor-class cruiser|''Interdictor''-class cruiser]] and the [[Centurion-class battlecruiser/Legends|''Centurion''-class battlecruiser]] were employed by Galactic Republic and later served in the navy of the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]] established by [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]].<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /><ref name="KOTORCG" /> Examples of these ships included the [[Leviathan (Interdictor-class cruiser)|''Leviathan'']]<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /> and the [[Ravager (Centurion-class)|''Ravager'']].<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>

The first design explicitly referred to as a "Star Destroyer", was the [[Harrower-class dreadnought|''Harrower''-class dreadnought]] of the resurgent [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. This design originated with [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Odile Vaiken]] as part of the Empire's military build-up in the 1,300 years that preceded the [[Great Galactic War]].<ref name="T11" />
These ships eventually fought in this 28-year long conflict against the Republic.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>

===Clone Wars-developments===
[[File:Acclamator-side-landed.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The ''Acclamator''-class [[Assault ship/Legends|assault ship]] circa [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], was a proto Star-Destroyer.]]
Star Destroyers that bore the distinctive wedge-shape, which came to be associated with the ship type, were in the service of the later [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] around the time of the Clone Wars. The two most famous designs at the time were the [[Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory I'']]- and [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator'']]-classes, which were considered massive. Other Republic Star Destroyers, like the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperator'']]- and [[Tector-class Star Destroyer|''Tector'']]-classes, became infamous for their service in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> The new Star Destroyer designs were born from the success of the [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship/Legends|''Acclamator''-class assault ship]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref><ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> In addition, then-Supreme Chancellor of the Republic and future Galactic Emperor Palpatine mentioned in his Sith compendium, the Book of Sith, that the Star Destroyers developed during this time also shared similarities with the ''Harrower''-class dreadnought.<ref name="Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>

===Imperial and New Republic usage===
During the time of the Empire, many smaller and less independent dagger-shaped ships, such as the [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Immobilizer 418 cruiser]]<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> and the [[Broadside-class cruiser kdb-1|''Broadside''-class cruiser]], were often compared to small Star Destroyers without being classified as one themselves. In the ''Broadside''{{'s}} case, it was downgraded from 'Star Destroyer' to 'cruiser', due to its lack of defensive power and mobility.<ref name="TFUCG" /> In large part because of a Star Destroyer's capabilities, [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], the leader of the Rebel Alliance, noted that if the Empire fragmented after Endor, it would pose the risk of any Imperial commander with access to a Star Destroyer becoming a warlord.<ref name="IHB">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

While Star Destroyers served as the heaviest combatants in many fleets composed of frigates and down-scaled cruisers, they performed an escort role when in the presence of specialized battleships found in the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]],<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> or larger Imperial warships such as the ''Executor''-class.<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations1" />
Both the Republic<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> and the Empire maintained a higher-tier system of vessels heavier and more powerful than Star Destroyers, categorized from [[Battlecruiser/Legends|Battlecruisers]] to [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnoughts]].<ref name="TEGTW" /> Building on the popularity the Star Destroyers gained in the Clone Wars, and the name of the "[[Super-class Star Destroyer|''Super''-class Star Destroyer]],"<ref name="Starship Battles Preview 1">{{SWMiniCite|set=Starship Battles|parent=1}} {{C|rulebook}}</ref> many of these heavy vessels were referred to in military colloquialism as "[[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyers]]" (sometimes omitting the "Super" prefix).<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations1" /> The Imperial Navy had around 25,000 ISDs alone throughout its existence.<ref name="JFT">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/23039847571/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-7|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 7}}</ref>

The New Republic also used the dagger-shape in their later Star Destroyer designs. However, not all vessels known as Star Destroyers adhered to the dagger aesthetic.<ref name="Cracken's Threat Dossier">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref>

[[File:PellaeonClassStarDestroyer-SeanCooke.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Three [[Pellaeon-class Star Destroyer|''Pellaeon''-class Star Destroyers]] circa [[137 ABY]].]]

Notable Star Destroyer-manufacturers through the ages included [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]],<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /><ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations1" /><ref name="Dark Empire Sourcebook">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> [[Rendili StarDrive/Legends|Rendili StarDrive]],<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook1" /> and the [[Republic Engineering Corporation]].<ref name="Cracken's Threat Dossier" />

===Later iterations===
Even though the Galactic Alliance continued to use and produce Star Destroyers, they later decided to name their new ships "battle carriers" in order to avoid reminding people of the old Imperial terror symbols.<ref name="Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref> By the time of the [[Sith–Imperial War]], the resurgent [[Fel Empire|Empire]] utilized the [[Pellaeon-class Star Destroyer|''Pellaeon''-class Star Destroyer]], which was described as one of the largest and most powerful warships of its time,<ref name="SOTG07" /> with unparalleled weapons-systems.<ref name="Star Wars: Legacy" /> The Sith Empire led by [[Darth Krayt]] later constructed the much bigger and heavily armed [[Imperious-class Star Destroyer]], the [[Alliance (Imperious-class)|''Imperious'']], which was stolen by the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]] led by [[Gar Stazi]] when it became operational.<ref name="SWL:I">''[[Star Wars: Legacy: Indomitable]]''</ref>

==Known designs==
===''Aggressor''-class Star Destroyer===
[[File:Aggressor_destroyer.jpg|thumb|250px|The ''Aggressor''-class]]
{{Main|Aggressor-class Star Destroyer}}
The ''Aggressor''-class Star Destroyer was an experimental design, whose plans and prototype vessel were stolen by the [[Zann Consortium/Legends|Zann Consortium]] and modified. The ''Aggressor''-class vessels went on to serve as one of the Consortium's most powerful capital ships.

===''Bakura''-class destroyer===
[[File:BakuraDestroyer.jpg|thumb|250px|The ''Bakura''-class]]
{{Main|Bakura-class destroyer}}
The ''Bakura''-class Star Destroyer was created by [[Bakura/Legends|Bakura]] after the [[Invasion of Bakura]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. It was built around an ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer's annihilation reactor and was 850 meters long. Three destroyers participated in the [[Battle of Centerpoint Station (Corellian Crisis)|Battle of Centerpoint Station]] in [[18 ABY/Legends|18 ABY]].

===Chiss Star Destroyer===
{{Main|Chiss Star Destroyer}}
Chiss Star Destroyers were needle-shaped warships 1,000 meters long, built by the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] and armed with [[maser]]s. They participated in the [[Swarm War]] against the [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]] in [[36 ABY]]. The [[Empire of the Hand]] utilized Chiss Star Destroyers in the [[Battle over Exodo II]] in [[44 ABY]].

===''Gladiator''-class Star Destroyer===
[[File:GladiatorClassStarDestroyer-SWArmada.png|thumb|250px|The ''Gladiator''-class]]
{{Main|Gladiator-class Star Destroyer/Legends}}
The ''Gladiator''-class was a small Star Destroyer class used by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to subjugate outlying systems and enforce order on Outer Rim worlds not justifying the need for larger vessels. It was 600 meters long, and had a large hangar area towards the front of the vessel, with a hangar bay opening at the bow.

===''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer===
The [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class]] consisted of several Star Destroyer models built by [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] over several decades.

====''Imperator/Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer====
[[File:Imperial-I-SD-ANH.jpg|thumb|250px|An ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer.]]
{{Main|Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends}}
The 1,600-meter-long ''Imperator''-class was created early in the Clone Wars, but only saw widespread deployment after the rise of the Galactic Empire. Following the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], the class was renamed to ''Imperial'', but the original name was used in some official documents. It came to symbolize the tyranny of Imperial rule and was used throughout the galaxy for many decades, even long after the fall of the Empire and the establishment of both the New Republic and later the Galactic Alliance, who appropriated many vessels and used them in their own navies.

====''Imperator II/Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer====
[[File:ISD.jpg|thumb|250px|The ''Imperial II''-class]]
{{Main|Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends}}
The ''Imperial II''-class was fielded years after the first model, with some cosmetic differences. It became the norm for the Imperial Navy, with some ''Imperial I''s retrofitted to be more similar to the second generation.

===''Imperious''-class Star Destroyer===
[[File:Alliance_flagship.jpg|thumb|250px|The ''Imperious''-class]]
{{Main|Imperious-class Star Destroyer}}
The ''Imperious''-class Star Destroyer [[Alliance (Imperious-class)|''Imperious'']] was built by the [[Mon Calamari Shipyards/Legends|Mon Calamari Shipyards]] for [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]]. It was later stolen by the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]] upon completion and turned into their flagship.

===''Interdictor''-class Star Destroyer===
[[File:InterdictorClassSD-EGTW.png|thumb|250px|Some Star Destroyers possessed gravity-well projectors, capable of inhibiting hyperspace travel, such as the ''Interdictor''-class.]]
{{Main|Interdictor-class Star Destroyer/Legends}}
The 1,600-meter-long ''Interdictor''-class Star Destroyer comprised several designs of Star Destroyers fitted with [[Gravity well projector/Legends|gravity well projectors]] based on the ones from the smaller [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Immobilizer 418 cruiser]].

===''Nebula/Defender''-class Star Destroyer===
[[File:Nebula-classStarDestroyer-SotGSE.png|250px|thumb|The high cost of the ''Nebula''-class Star Destroyer meant few ships were built.]]
{{Main|Nebula-class Star Destroyer}}
The ''Nebula''-class, also known as ''Defender''-class, was a class of expensive and powerful warships. They were only 1,040 meters long, but their firepower was strong enough to dominate any known Star Destroyer class at the time and could take on some Super Star Destroyers as well. While smaller than other Destroyers they were packed with armament, at the expense of crew endurance. Because of their power requirements, they were very expensive and had a relatively small production run. Despite this, they performed well as [[Core Worlds/Legends|core]] fleets during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].

===''Pellaeon''-class Star Destroyer===
[[File:Pellaeon-classStarDestroyer-SotGSE.png|thumb|250px|Like the [[Interdictor-class cruiser|''Interdictor''-class cruiser]], [[Harrower-class dreadnought]],
[[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]] and [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] before it, the ''Pellaeon''-class Star Destroyer was the mainstay capital ship of its era. It was fielded over 100 years after the destruction of the Death Star.]]
{{Main|Pellaeon-class Star Destroyer}}
The ''Pellaeon''-class was built over 100 years after the Battle of Endor and the beginning of the downfall of the first Galactic Empire. It was made by KDY for the Fel Empire, and was based on the ''Imperial''-class and also incorporated some elements of the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]]. It later served as the signature vessel of [[Darth Krayt]]'s Empire.

===Procursator===
[[File:Procursatorblownup.png|thumb|250px|The 1,200 meter ''Procursator''-class]]
{{Main|Procursator-class Star Destroyer}}
The ''Procursator''-class was a class used by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].

===''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer===
{{Main|Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends}}

The ''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer was a capital ship design used during the Clone Wars by the Confederacy of Independent Systems. Some were identified under the name Separatist Star Destroyers.

===''Rejuvenator''-class Star Destroyer===
{{Main|Rejuvenator-class Star Destroyer}}
The ''Rejuvenator''-class was a class that fought during the tail-end of the Yuuzhan Vong War in [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]].

===''Republic''-class Star Destroyer===
[[File:Rsd.jpg|thumb|250px|The ''Republic''-class]]
{{Main|Republic-class Star Destroyer}}
The ''Republic''-class had a long design phase, beginning as a new warship project early on in the New Republic but only fielded in limited amounts after [[Operation Shadow Hand]]. Ships were distributed to several task forces at some point before the [[Black Fleet Crisis]]. They were 1,250 meters long and despite being bigger than the ''Nebula''-class, were weaker than them, being less powerful than an ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer.

===''Secutor''-class Star Destroyer===
{{Main|Secutor-class Star Destroyer/Legends}}
The ''Secutor''-class served the Galactic Empire at [[Naval Station Validusia/Legends|Naval Station ''Validusia'']] and the [[Dark Empire]] at [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] as a support ship for the larger Imperial warships. Although its size technically qualified it under the Star Cruiser subclass of Star Battlecruiser under length requirements, its comparative lack of heavy armaments and [[Carrier/Legends|carrier]]-like qualities had it retain the Star Destroyer classification.

===''Sorannan''-class Star Destroyer===
{{Main|Sorannan-class Star Destroyer}}
The ''Sorannan''-class was a weapons and engine testbed for the Galactic Empire. The only known representative of the class, the [[Rakehell (Sorannan-class)|''Rakehell'']], originally known as the ''EX-F'', was attached to [[Sixth Negative Regions|Black Sword Command]] before being captured during the [[Yevethan Uprising]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. During the climax of the [[Black Fleet Crisis]] in [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]], the captured Imperials of [[Camp Pa'aal Squadron]] seized control of the [[Black Fleet]], including the ''EX-F'', and fled to the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. Upon learning of the destruction of [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] [[11 ABY/Legends|six years earlier]], Camp Pa'aal Squadron scattered, with the newly renamed ''Rakehell'' ending up in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]], and ultimately being destroyed during the [[Battle of Anx Minor]] later that year.

===''Tector''-class Star Destroyer===
{{Main|Tector-class Star Destroyer}}
The 1,600 meter ''Tector''-class was a hangarless design that was built during the Clone Wars, but only widely fielded during the reign of the Galactic Empire. Like the ''Imperial''-class, it saw service for decades.

===''Turbulent''-class Star Destroyer===
{{Main|Turbulent-class Star Destroyer}}
The ''Turbulent''-class was a small type of Star Destroyer built by the Imperial Remnant in [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]] and was fielded towards the end of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]].

===''Venator''-class Star Destroyer===
[[File:Venator2-SWE.png|thumb|250px|A ''Venator''-class painted in Republic colors.]]
{{Main|Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends}}
The ''Venator''-class was 1,137 meters long, and had the dual role of warship and carrier during the Clone Wars. They served as Jedi flagships during the Wars, and were thus heavily linked to them, leading to their gradual abandonment by the Galactic Empire. Their other weakness was long hangar bay doors, which were vulnerable while opening and closing.

===''Victory''-class Star Destroyer===
The ''Victory''-class consisted of several Star Destroyer models initially built by [[Rendili StarDrive/Legends|Rendili StarDrive]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

====''Victory I''-class Star Destroyer====
[[File:VicStarI-EaW.jpg|250px|thumb|The ''Victory''-class Star Destroyer was a rushed production and subsequently suffered for it in naval plans.]]
{{Main|Victory I-class Star Destroyer/Legends}}

The ''Victory I'' was rushed out of development as part of the [[Victor Initiative Project]] between KDY and Rendili StarDrive. They were 900 meters long and were not as well-made as other Star Destroyer designs, despite early successful campaigns like the hunt for the [[Bulwark Fleet]] during the Clone Wars. The ''Victory''-class still managed to serve for many decades and for successive galactic governments despite its flaws.

====''Victory II''-class Star Destroyer====
{{Main|Victory II-class Star Destroyer/Legends}}
The ''Victory II''-class was made right after the establishment of the Galactic Empire, and was produced in even fewer numbers than the ''Victory I''.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:RMQ-stardestroyer.png|thumb|left|250px|Concept art by Ralph McQuarrie of Star Destroyers over [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]]]
In [[The Star Wars rough draft|The Star Wars: Rough Draft]], a [[Stardestroyer]] is a small, two-man craft. The final film used this term for large capital ships, and all contemporaneous written sources spelled it as two words. Nonetheless, the subtitles on the [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] DVDs transcribed the term as "stardestroyer."

The sounds for the Star Destroyer came from a broken air conditioner in a hotel room in White Sands Proving Range, New Mexico. Sounds from the Goodyear blimp were mixed in to create the iconic rumble of a Star Destroyer.<ref name="TSOSW">''[[The Sounds of Star Wars]]''</ref>

According to ''[[Star Wars and History]]'', Star Destroyers were comparable to the [[Wikipedia:Boeing B-52 Stratofortress|Boeing B-52 Stratofortress]], which dropped more bombs during the Vietnam War than all the bombs dropped during World War II.

On the commentary track of the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']] DVD, [[George Lucas]] referred to General Grievous's ship, a [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer]], as a "Star Destroyer." This might mean that the term "Star Destroyer" is not supposed to be restricted to dagger-shaped warships, which fits with the existence of the ''Bakura''-class. Or this might have been just a generalization.

The term "Star Destroyer" is used both for different classes of destroyers and as a general term for most dagger-shaped warships in use by the Empire, from smaller frigates like the ''[[Demolisher]]'' to giant dreadnoughts like the ''Executor'' and the [[Eclipse (Eclipse-class)|''Eclipse'']]. This has created some ambiguity, as many sources describe ships only as a "Star Destroyer" or "Imperial Star Destroyer." Since many stories have historically focused on the 1,600-meter-long ''Imperial''-class, it is used as a default reference unless stated otherwise.

In the endnotes for ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', Jason Fry mentioned that he initially had trouble coming up with a class for the various Star Destroyers, until he eventually settled on making Star Destroyer a ship class, due to it being used synonymously with a big capital ship, which likewise implied a ship class.<ref name="EGWendnotes">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/21215590247/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-3|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 3}}</ref>

Lego has released a set featuring the Star Destroyer. It includes stormtroopers, Darth Vader, R2-Q5, Grand Moff Tarkin, Imperial Officers, and Royal Guards.
